tasks.short: Balance gameplay from play numbers and a signed note

steps.what: Export gameplay rows for one build
Read gameplay numbers before balancing
Draft balance changes that cite a level
Decide how to adjust gameplay balance
File the signed balance version
Apply the signed balance in the build

tasks.design: Play rows for a level land on a {BI} view with level id, fail rate and time, and no tester name. A {DOCS} note lists those rows and leaves the new number blank. The game designer decides how to adjust the gameplay and signs one balance version. The programmer changes the build only from that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fail rates lived in chat and the proposed numbers lived in a private spreadsheet, so a note could not show which level it referred to.
tasks.enabler_now: A play export can carry a level id, a fail rate and a time, which a note can list without naming a tester.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a hard moment should stay hard is a design call, not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides which numbers change and which difficulty stays.

ambition.what: Retune a level the same week its fail rate stays high, not only at the milestone review

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting screenshots, more time on the balance call. The designer can refuse a change that cites no level id.

reach.task: Apply the signed balance numbers in the build
reach.learn: Which level ids have a signed number and which are still open

evidence.claim: In a mid-size studio this task is a spreadsheet of numbers plus a meeting. The hard part is the balance call, not the formatting.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. These play rows store a level id and a fail rate, not a named tester.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to a live game build is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed balance version is filed. Changing the build is the programmer's later act, done while a person watches.
Input contract: level id, fail rate, median time, attempt count, build id. Producer is the programmer's play export. A row with no level id stays on a manual list and is not cited.
The meeting prior fits the decision. Gathering numbers is spreadsheet work. Use the dashboard's own filters before custom code.
Play rows do not name testers. A design that scores named staff needs works-council consent and is out of this task.
unknowns: Whether today's export already stores tester names.
Who may sign a balance version when the designer is away.
Which levels have no stable id.
research_questions: What share of play rows lack a level id?
How often does the signed number differ from the designer's first mark?

already_counted.description: Designer edits a weak balance note before the call
The balance call stays with the designer

incremental.description: Keep the balance note headings aligned when a new stat appears
Programmer fixes play rows the view rejects

approvals.approved_version: balance version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most play notes stay free text, so the sheet rarely cites a row and the balance meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes clean rows, but every balance call and every build change stays with a person. No unattended live change is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Devise missions and file a signed outline

steps.what: Devise the puzzles and the challenges
Name the missions to be encountered
Fill the missions outline from named fields
Sign the missions outline in review
File the signed missions outline

tasks.design: The designer writes goal, constraint, fail state and reward for the missions before any page is filled. A {DOCS} template places only those fields under the outline headings and leaves a blank where a field is empty. The designer signs one outline version, and that version is what the programmer builds.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mission ideas lived in meeting notes, so an outline could not tell a chosen fail state from a sentence someone might still change.
tasks.enabler_now: A mission can be stored as a few named fields, and a template can refuse a heading that has no field.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the puzzle is fair, surprising or worth playing is a design judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer devises the puzzles and decides the fail state.
tasks.altitude: The outline takes less rewriting. The designer keeps the puzzles and can refuse an outline that invented a field.

reach.task: Build the encounter from the signed mission outline
reach.learn: Which missions have a signed fail state and which headings are still blank

evidence.claim: Devising missions, challenges and puzzles is a creative act in a mid-size studio. The page that records goal, constraint and fail state is the part with a stable shape.
A document template can place named fields under headings. It cannot decide whether a puzzle is good, so the sign-off stays with the designer.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed mission outline is filed. Building the encounter is the programmer's later work.
Input contract: mission id, goal, constraint, fail state, reward, estimated minutes. Producer is the game designer. If a field is empty the template leaves that heading blank and does not invent it.
Use the document store's own templates before custom code. The meeting prior includes workshop time that is really the devising, which stays manual.
unknowns: Who else may sign an outline when the designer is away.
Whether mission ids already exist for the current game.
research_questions: What share of outlines are rewritten after the first play?
How often is the fail state still blank at sign-off?

already_counted.description: Devising the puzzles stays with the designer
Designer corrects a heading the template left weak

incremental.description: Revise outline headings when a new mission type appears

approvals.approved_version: missions outline version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the designer still writes most outlines as free prose, so the template fills little and devising is unchanged. The high case assumes the fields are used, but devising the puzzles and the sign-off stay manual. Building the encounter is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create storylines, mechanics and character biographies

steps.what: Create the mechanics and the features
Write character motives and storylines
Draft biographies from the character fields
Sign the features and the biographies
File the signed features version

tasks.design: The designer states feature id, mechanic summary, character name and motive on a {DOCS} form. A template writes the storylines and biographies only by placing those fields, and leaves a blank where a field is empty. The designer signs one features version. The artist and the programmer take that version and do not take an unsigned page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Story notes and character pages were separate documents, so a draft could not tell a chosen motive from a line that was still a guess.
tasks.enabler_now: A feature can carry an id, a mechanic summary and a character motive that a page can quote.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the story and the role-play are worth making is a creative judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer creates the mechanics and decides the character's motive.

ambition.what: Re-check a character motive whenever the mechanic changes, not only at the franchise pitch

tasks.altitude: Less time on blank biography pages. The designer can reject a page that adds a motive they did not write.

reach.task: Draw the character from the signed biography
reach.learn: Which motives are signed and which biographies are still blank

evidence.claim: Storylines, mechanics and character biographies in a mid-size studio are written by the designer. The page layout is the part with a stable shape.
A template can place a motive the designer already wrote. It should not invent a motive, a mechanic or a storyline beat.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed features version is filed. Art and code are later tasks.

Input contract: feature id, mechanic summary, character name, motive, storyline beats the designer wrote, franchise name if any. Producer is the game designer. An empty motive leaves the biography section blank.
Use the document store's own templates before custom code. The meeting prior includes pitches that stay as conversations outside this filing path.
unknowns: Who may sign a feature version when the designer is away.
Whether character names are already fixed by an earlier pitch.
research_questions: What share of biography pages are rewritten after the mechanic changes?
How often is the motive still blank at sign-off?

already_counted.description: Creating the mechanics stays with the designer
Designer rewrites a biography line the template misplaced

incremental.description: Update biography headings when a new character role appears

approvals.approved_version: features version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes storylines and biographies stay free prose, so the template fills little. The high case assumes the fields are used, but creating the mechanics and signing the pages stay manual. Drawing the character is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Solicit feedback and integrate it into the design

steps.what: Solicit feedback from design staff
Obtain technical feedback from staff
Add art feedback on the design
Log feedback against the original design

loop.input: comment text and the known design ids
loop.output: comments that each cite one design id, plus a manual list
loop.check: Every kept comment cites a design id that exists
loop.stop: One pass, then comments with no design id stay on the manual list
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments mix an id with chatty prose, so a keyword split drops the id or keeps the chatter

steps.what: Decide which feedback to integrate
File the signed feedback decisions

tasks.design: Design and technical staff send comments on a {WORKFLOW} form with speaker, design id and the comment. A bounded pass in {DOCS} keeps only comments that cite a known design id. The game designer decides which ones to integrate into the original design and signs that change list. The meeting itself stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comments arrived in meetings and chat with no design id, so a list could not show which note they referred to.
tasks.enabler_now: A comment can carry a design id and a speaker, which a list can group without judging the comment.
tasks.still_hard: Whether feedback improves the original design is a judgement, and asking for it is a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The designer chooses which comments to integrate and which to leave.

ambition.what: Accept or reject each feedback item in the same week, not in a monthly pile

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The designer spends less time reconstructing who said what, and can refuse a change that cites no design id.

reach.task: Change the build only for feedback the designer accepted
reach.learn: Which comments were integrated and which were declined

evidence.claim: Soliciting feedback in a mid-size studio is a conversation. The written list of comments is the part with a stable shape, and integrating a comment is still a design judgement.
A bounded pass can keep a comment that cites a known design id and flag the rest. It cannot decide whether the original design should change.

assumptions: Focal role is the game designer. The task ends when a signed change list is filed. The conversation is not replaced by the form.
Input contract: design id, speaker role, comment text, date. Producer is the programmer, the artist or the designer. Comments with no design id stay on a manual list.
The meeting prior is accepted. The form only records what was said. Use the workflow tool's own form before custom code.
unknowns: Which design ids exist for the current build.
Who may accept a comment when the designer is away.
research_questions: What share of comments arrive with no design id?
How often does the signed list drop the first suggestion?

already_counted.description: Asking for feedback stays a conversation
Choosing what to integrate stays with the designer

incremental.description: Keep the comment form aligned when design ids change
Programmer and artist resubmit comments the list flags

approvals.approved_version: change list signed for this design id set

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most comments stay as unmarked chat, so the list rarely sticks and the meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes the form is used, but soliciting feedback and choosing what to integrate stay manual. Build changes by the programmer are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The designer stops reformatting mission pages and feature notes, and spends the week on balance calls, puzzle ideas and which feedback to keep.
reach: Programmers receive a signed balance note and a filed mission outline instead of a chat thread.
Artists draw from a signed character biography instead of a motive that was still a guess.
skills_to_grow: Write a balance change as a level id, a number and a reason a sheet can check.
State a mission as goal, constraint, fail state and reward before any outline is filled.
Separate a feedback comment from a change that is allowed into the original design.
role.ambitious_version: Each milestone opens with a signed balance note, a current mission outline and a short list of accepted feedback.
